Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, could you turn this into a clear prompt for a case-specific volunteer handoff note, not a general repair cafe guide. it’s one fictional episode at the North Quay Library Repair Cafe on saturday 18 october 2025, during the 10 to 1 session. the object is a brass desk lamp, brought in by Mara Bell. it belonged to her aunt and has a dark green shade with a small crease near the rim. the lamp is on the intake table at the moment, unplugged, and nobody has tested or powered it. please keep that status straight: don’t write as though anyone has already opened it, found a fault, repaired it, or confirmed it safe. Mara said, “It worked last winter, but I don't know who changed the cord.” Keep that as an ordinary quote in the note, word for word, and don’t turn it into evidence that the lamp works now.

The note is for Jo, the volunteer who may take the lamp to the back bench after the intake discussion. Jo has basic electrical repair experience and the cafe has a plug-in continuity and insulation-resistance tester, but don’t make Jo sound like a qualified electrician or say that the tester has been used. There are other volunteers at the bench, and the cafe uses a red tray for items that must remain unplugged. Mara has not said whether she wants to wait or leave the lamp; she asked whether the cord could be changed during this session. The note should make clear that replacing the two-core flex and plug is a possible action only under the inspection and test condition below, rather than presenting it as the default or promising that it can be done.

The condition is that, before replacing the cord, Jo must inspect the lampholder, switch, and accessible internal wiring and find no heat damage at any of those points. The continuity and insulation-resistance tests must also pass on the cafe tester. State both parts of the condition, not one or the other. If any of those parts shows heat damage, either test fails, or a required check cannot be completed, Jo must not replace the flex or plug and must not energize the lamp. No shortcuts based on Mara’s memory of it working last winter. If the condition does hold, the requested action is to replace the two-core flex and plug; the note can say to record that this is the conditional task, but don’t claim it has happened or that the lamp then works. If it does not hold, give a genuinely different useful next action: leave the lamp unplugged in the red tray, make a non-powered handoff note describing only what was observed and which checks failed or could not be completed, and refer the unresolved electrical work to a qualified electrician. Don’t treat that fallback as the main repair, and don’t tell the volunteer to keep testing until it passes.

Please make the note practical for this exact handoff, with enough context that Jo can tell which lamp and owner it concerns. Include the intake facts that the lamp is brass, has a dark green shade with a crease near its rim, came from Mara’s aunt, is currently unplugged and untested, and that the cord’s history is unknown. The quote belongs with those intake facts. Don’t add a diagnosis, a parts price, a source for a replacement cord, a completed test result, permission that Mara hasn’t given, or an outcome. We don’t yet know whether the flex is original, whether the crease affects anything, or whether the lamp can be safely repaired here. Keep uncertainty specific to those unknowns rather than adding a stock warning paragraph.

The note should distinguish what is known at intake from what Jo would need to check at the bench. It may mention the library’s small back bench, where the tester is kept, and the red tray, but don’t imply the lamp has been moved there already. There is also a general hand tool drawer beside the bench; it isn’t important to list every tool or give step-by-step wiring instructions. A numbered section would be natural for the two possible paths: first, proceed with cord replacement only if the whole condition is met; second, if it is not met or cannot be checked, stop and use the non-powered handoff alternative. Make the conditional relationship unmistakable and keep both paths in the note.

Mara said she can wait until 11:40 if a volunteer is able to discuss the next step with her, but she may need to leave before then. Don’t assume she will stay, and don’t say she has agreed to a later pickup. The cafe closes at 1, and any item left after its owner goes is stored in the lockable cabinet until the next monthly session; include this as practical handoff information, not as a claim that Mara has left the lamp. The session coordinator is Dev, who can help arrange a conversation with a qualified electrician if the fallback is needed. Dev is coordinating volunteers today, not making a safety judgment on the lamp.

Please write one concise but useful case-specific volunteer handoff note in connected paragraphs, not a dialogue, a completed repair report, or a broad safety policy. Use a short heading, an ordinary quote, and a numbered section if that fits naturally. Put a distinct practical detail in the final paragraph, such as the waiting window, closing time, or cabinet arrangement, rather than repeating the condition there. Return only the finished handoff note, with no preface or explanation.", "output": "Write one concise, case-specific volunteer handoff note for the fictional North Quay Library Repair Cafe session on Saturday, 18 October 2025, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The note is for Jo, the volunteer who may take an item from intake to the back bench. Use connected paragraphs, a short heading, and an ordinary quote. A numbered section for the two possible paths is appropriate. Return only the finished handoff note, with no preface or explanation; do not write a general repair-cafe guide, dialogue, completed repair report, or broad safety policy.

Identify the item as Mara Bell’s brass desk lamp, which belonged to her aunt. It has a dark green shade with a small crease near the rim. At intake it is unplugged and has not been opened, tested, or powered. Include Mara’s exact words: “It worked last winter, but I don't know who changed the cord.” Treat this as her account, not as proof that the lamp works now. The cord’s history is unknown. Mara asked whether its cord could be changed during the session, but has not said whether she will wait or leave. Do not invent a diagnosis, repair, test result, safety finding, permission, or outcome. It is not known whether the flex is original, whether the crease affects anything, or whether the lamp can be safely repaired at the cafe.

Address Jo as a volunteer with basic electrical repair experience, not as a qualified electrician. The cafe has a plug-in continuity and insulation-resistance tester at the small back bench, a red tray for items that must remain unplugged, and a general hand-tool drawer beside the bench. These are available resources; do not imply the lamp has been moved to the bench, the tester has been used, or any inspection has taken place. Do not list every tool or provide step-by-step wiring instructions.

Set out both possible paths clearly:

1. Jo may replace the lamp’s two-core flex and plug only if, before replacement, inspection of the lampholder, switch, and accessible internal wiring finds no heat damage at any of those points, and both the continuity and insulation-resistance tests pass on the cafe tester. Both the inspection condition and the test condition must be met. Present this as a conditional possible action, not the default or a promise. Do not say the checks have been done, the cord has been replaced, or the lamp works afterward.
2. If any of those locations shows heat damage, either test fails, or a required check cannot be completed, Jo must not replace the flex or plug and must not energize the lamp. The useful alternative is to leave it unplugged in the red tray, prepare a non-powered handoff note describing only what was observed and which checks failed or could not be completed, and refer unresolved electrical work to a qualified electrician. Do not make this fallback the primary repair, or suggest repeated testing until a pass is obtained. Mara’s recollection that the lamp worked last winter does not change the condition.

Keep intake information distinct from checks Jo would need to make at the bench. Do not claim that the lamp has already been taken there. Include the practical handoff details without assuming what Mara will do: she can wait until 11:40 if a volunteer can discuss the next step with her, but may need to leave earlier. The cafe closes at 1 p.m.; an item left after its owner goes is stored in the lockable cabinet until the next monthly session. Dev is the session coordinator and can help arrange a conversation with a qualified electrician if the fallback is needed, but Dev is coordinating volunteers, not making a safety judgment about the lamp. End with a distinct practical detail, such as the waiting window, closing time, or cabinet arrangement, rather than repeating the repair condition."}]
